name: Nathan Hodgson
inspiration: instagram.com/nathanhodgson.ai — the 'replayed tutorial' reel. Refs pulled from his last 10 reels (Aug 3-17 2026: DcJ0T19xsFx, DcHRrxNReQv, DcEfmJeutHp, DcCSsqsxGW8, Db_uV82x_2_, Db80jdBxmNc, Db6G_VhO8lh, Db3dRm9s1yg, Db1Ba0iu5fy, Dbydve0OqNc). Warm cream stage that is never flat, ONE orange accent, and interfaces that are REDRAWN (not screen-captured) and execute themselves while he talks: prompts type themselves, counters run, badges flip to done. Permanent top/bottom sandwich with a hard seam at ~52%, one-word pill captions, and the same violet Comment end-card on 10 reels out of 10. Reference frames in references/.
summary: The short-form 'proof reel' style. Use for 35-55s vertical tool demos where a redrawn UI plays its own sequence above the talking head — the closest published analog to the user's reels, and the short-form complement to Dan Kieft (11). PLAYBOOK.md is the full A-to-Z edit recipe (speech-to-shot table, in-shot cadence rules) with a real reel decomposed shot by shot. Pick this style for WORKFLOWS (step sequences to replay); pick Nick Saraev (13) for tool NEWS.
format: vertical reels 9:16 (1080x1920). Not built for long-form.

palette.notes: ONE accent only (orange). Green and blue are UI statuses, not accents. The violet gradient exists only on the end-card. Ink is warm brown-black, never #000. Sampled per-pixel from the refs. Mirrored in tokens.css.

fonts.notes: Display = heavy grotesque CAPS, tightly tracked (-0.035em), titles only; numbers inside titles are orange and count up. Poppins (geometric) carries everything else including the one-word captions — it is what makes the style read 'product'. JetBrains Mono for values, counters, paths, statuses only, never a sentence. No serif anywhere.

motion: Three speeds. POP (everything that arrives) back.out(1.8) ~0.32s. RUN (whatever executes: typing 45ms/char, counters, progress bars) strictly linear — it is a machine, not an animation. FLOAT (the cream stage's blurred blocks) ~9s drift, never resolved. The defining rule: redrawn UIs PLAY A SEQUENCE in causal order (prompt types → status appears → result rows drop in → badges flip → counter runs). Nothing is 'presented'; everything happens.
transitions: Hard cuts. The frame sandwich has a hard seam at 44-60% height (graphic above, talking head below) — never a gradient. Full-frame graphic moments last 2-3s max before the face returns. Every reel ends on the violet Comment card at -1 to -3s.

pacing.notes: Measured across the 10 reels (scene>0.25 detection). Half the speed of Nick Saraev — each shot must hold long enough for a UI sequence to play. Do not speed this style up.

cards.notes: The style's stamp: small orange asterisk, tight CAPS title, 43%-wide 7px gradient rule drawing left-to-right in 0.32s. If the title contains a number, it is orange and counts up.

THE signature. A redrawn dark app card on the cream stage plays its causal sequence: prompt types itself (45ms/char) → status line pops → result rows drop (stagger 0.18s) → badges flip to green ✓ → counter runs linearly with the progress bar. Composer bar stays inert at the bottom as context proof.
Three white rows max, icon chip left, bold label + grey sub, MONO value right-aligned. Rows arrive from below one by one, 0.18s apart. Never a sentence in the value slot.

The mandatory ending, present in 10/10 source reels. Violet gradient panel over the top ~25% of frame, 'Comment' in white geometric, full-width white pill mimicking a real IG comment field (keyword in REGULAR weight — the only non-bold type in the style), share glyph right.

One word at a time in a translucent grey pill (rgba(37,27,21,.56), radius 14), white bold geometric, centered just below the sandwich seam (~56% height) — never on the mouth. Word swaps at spoken onset with a 0.16s micro-pop.

His annotation gesture: zoom a real document to 200-300% and sweep the native browser text selection (#2D5ECB) across the phrase as he says it. No drawn frames, no arrows — the selection IS the highlight. The exact inverse of Nick Saraev's neon frame; never mix the two.
